title: Jeffrey Archer
wiki_lead:
Jeffrey Howard Archer, Baron Archer of Weston-super-Mare (15 April 1940 – 5 October 2026) was an English novelist and politician. He served as Member of Parliament (MP) for Louth, Lincolnshire, from the 1969 by-election until 1974, when he did not seek re-election after almost going bankrupt. Archer revived his fortunes as a novelist with his third novel Kane and Abel (1979). It remains one of the best-selling books in the world, with an estimated 34 million copies sold globally. Overall, his books have sold more than 320 million copies worldwide.
Archer returned to politics and was deputy chairman of the Conservative Party from 1985 to 1986; he resigned after the Daily Star newspaper accused him of paying money to a sex worker, Monica Coghlan. In 1987, he won a libel suit against the paper and was awarded large damages. He was made a life peer in 1992 and subsequently became the first Conservative to be selected as a candidate for mayor of London. He ended his candidacy in 1999 after it emerged that he had lied in the 1987 case. In 2001, he was sentenced to four years in prison for perjury and perverting the course of justice, ending his active political career. He was released early in 2003.
Archer retired from the House of Lords in 2024.

Early life
Jeffrey Howard Archer was born on 15 April 1940 at the City of London Maternity Hospital in Holloway, London. Shortly after Archer's birth, his family moved to Somerset, settling in Weston-super-Mare, where Archer spent most of his early life.
Archer's parents were William Archer (c. 1876–1956) and Lola Archer née Cook (1913–2001). William was 64 years old when Archer was born, and nearly 40 years his wife's senior.
William was a bigamist, fraudster, and conman who impersonated another William Archer, a deceased war medal holder. He was at different times employed as a chewing gum salesman in New York and a mortgage broker in London. In the latter capacity, he was charged at the Old Bailey with a series of fraud offences. On being released on bail, he absconded to the U.S. under the name of William Grimwood. In the U.S., William fathered a child, Rosemary Turner (21 June 1917 – 11 October 1986), Jeffrey's half-sister. In 1940, Rosemary married lawyer Brien McMahon, who went on to become a Democratic senator for Connecticut (1945–1952) and a contender for the Democratic presidential nomination in 1952. After McMahon's death that year, Rosemary married, in 1953, the Ambassador of Belgium to the United States, Baron Robert Silvercruys.
Archer's mother, Lola Archer (born Lola Cook, and later Lola Hayne), became the first female journalist at the family's local paper, The Weston & Somerset Mercury. At 17, Lola had an illegitimate child, a daughter named Wendy, who was given away for adoption. She later met William, and had second illegitimate child, a son named Jeffrey, who was also given away for adoption. grok_lead: Jeffrey Howard Archer, Baron Archer of Weston-super-Mare (15 April 1940 â 5 October 2026), was an English novelist and former politician renowned for his prolific output of bestselling fiction, with global sales exceeding 300 million copies across works published in over 100 countries. Elected as the Conservative Member of Parliament for Louth at age 29 in a 1969 by-election, he held the seat until 1974, when investment losses in a fraudulent Canadian venture pushed him toward bankruptcy and prompted his resignation. Archer later served as Deputy Chairman of the Conservative Party from 1985 to 1986 and was elevated to the peerage in 1992, but his political ambitions, including a 1999 candidacy for Mayor of London, were derailed by scandals. His literary career, launched with the 1976 novel Not a Penny More, Not a Penny Less, yielded 19 number-one fiction bestsellers, alongside successful plays and the non-fiction Prison Diaries series, the latter stemming from his 2001 conviction for perjury and perverting the course of justice in a 1987 libel case, for which he received a four-year sentence and served two years in prison. These events underscored Archer's trajectory of remarkable recoveries amid repeated controversies, including earlier financial improprieties that tested his resilience. Archer died suddenly and peacefully at his home on 5 October 2026, aged 86, between writing sessions. His publisher HarperCollins confirmed the news, noting that his final work was due to be unveiled that week.
